source: Context AI current concept catalog; research input, separate from the pinned development loadout

product.intent.definition: Define the outcome the work must achieve for its users.

product.audience.definition: Identify the people, agents, and systems that consume the result.

product.requirements.definition: Separate required behavior from preferences and assumptions.

product.constraints.definition: Record hard limits on time, cost, compatibility, and authority.

product.scope.definition: Bound the work and its completion criteria.

product.prioritization.definition: Order work by user value, risk, and dependencies.

product.tradeoffs.definition: Record consequential choices and their costs.

product.lifecycle.definition: Plan ownership, maintenance, deprecation, and removal.

research.discovery.definition: Find relevant primary sources and existing implementations.

research.prior_art.definition: Assess existing standards, native facilities, and maintained tools before building.

research.provenance.definition: Keep a claim traceable to its original source or observation.

research.credibility.definition: Judge source authority, independence, and applicability.

research.synthesis.definition: Combine evidence without laundering inference into fact.

research.decision.definition: Choose an owner for each responsibility with a review trigger.

research.freshness.definition: Assess evidence age against the volatility of the deciding claim.

research.licensing.definition: Establish reuse and redistribution rights for sources and software.

context.instructions.definition: Route durable instructions by authority and scope.

context.project_knowledge.definition: Retrieve project facts and decisions when relevant.

context.retrieval.definition: Select just enough source material for the current task.

context.skills.definition: Package repeatable procedures for on-demand use.

context.memory.definition: Preserve useful long-lived knowledge without treating recall as authority.

context.compression.definition: Retain decisions and constraints when shortening history.

context.budget.definition: Control the attention, token, and latency cost of supplied context.

context.provenance.definition: Trace context excerpts to their original material.

context.injection.definition: Keep untrusted content from becoming instructions.

context.adaptation.definition: Map shared guidance to a provider's actual instruction mechanism.

context.sync.definition: Detect drift between source material and derived context.

models.selection.definition: Choose a model for the task's required capabilities and constraints.

models.reasoning.definition: Set deliberation effort proportional to difficulty and stakes.

models.routing.definition: Map task attributes to a current model and fallback.

models.prompting.definition: Give clear tasks, constraints, inputs, and completion criteria.

models.tool_use.definition: Bound when and how a model may call tools.

models.structured_output.definition: Validate machine-consumed model output against a contract.

models.multimodal.definition: Select and verify image, audio, video, or text handling.

models.cost_latency.definition: Measure total time and cost at acceptable quality.

models.fallback.definition: Recover when a model is unavailable or fails the task.

models.eval.definition: Compare model behavior on representative tasks.

agents.decomposition.definition: Split work into independently checkable tasks when useful.

agents.orchestration.definition: Coordinate agent work, dependencies, and result assembly.

agents.delegation.definition: Delegate bounded work with a clear return contract.

agents.isolation.definition: Keep concurrent changes and experiments from interfering.

agents.state.definition: Persist the minimum state needed to resume or audit work.

agents.handoff.definition: Transfer constraints, evidence, and remaining work faithfully.

agents.recovery.definition: Resume safely after interruption or partial failure.

agents.autonomy.definition: Match independent action to the user's authorization and risk.

agents.oversight.definition: Reserve consequential choices for human judgment where needed.

integration.protocols.definition: Prefer interoperable protocols where they fit the job.

integration.mcp.definition: Connect model applications to tools and resources through MCP.

integration.plugins.definition: Distribute a cohesive set of capabilities across supported surfaces.

integration.hooks.definition: Run checks at supported lifecycle or tool events.

integration.commands.definition: Expose repeatable operations through native commands.

integration.api_contracts.definition: Define request, response, error, and compatibility behavior.

integration.authentication.definition: Establish identity and permissions for external systems.

integration.external_data.definition: Access external applications and data with explicit boundaries.

integration.workflow_capture.definition: Turn a demonstrated repeatable workflow into a reusable procedure.

architecture.boundaries.definition: Assign authority and responsibilities to clear components.

architecture.composition.definition: Combine existing components before adding a new platform.

architecture.patterns.definition: Select patterns for present needs and removal cost.

architecture.interfaces.definition: Keep component interfaces explicit and testable.

architecture.contracts.definition: State input, output, invariant, and failure conditions.

architecture.state.definition: Decide what state exists, who owns it, and how it changes.

architecture.effects.definition: Keep side effects visible and controlled.

architecture.idempotency.definition: Make retries safe where operations may repeat.

architecture.migration.definition: Evolve contracts and stored state without losing history.

architecture.portability.definition: Isolate provider or platform assumptions behind narrow adapters.

implementation.reuse.definition: Inspect existing code and libraries before writing a new mechanism.

implementation.dependencies.definition: Choose dependencies by fit, maintenance, and exit cost.

implementation.types.definition: Use type and schema checks to express useful invariants.

implementation.errors.definition: Make failures observable and recoverable at the right boundary.

implementation.configuration.definition: Keep runtime settings explicit and scoped.

implementation.comments.definition: Explain non-obvious intent and contracts without narrating code.

implementation.debugging.definition: Reproduce and localize faults before changing behavior.

implementation.refactoring.definition: Improve structure while preserving observable behavior.

data.modeling.definition: Represent entities, relationships, and constraints faithfully.

data.validation.definition: Reject malformed or out-of-contract data at a defined boundary.

data.lineage.definition: Track how data was sourced, transformed, and used.

data.persistence.definition: Choose durable storage and recovery semantics for the workload.

data.privacy.definition: Minimize sensitive data and define its permitted uses.

data.retention.definition: Set deletion and archival behavior for retained data.

data.portability.definition: Keep data exportable and avoid needless lock-in.

data.determinism.definition: Produce stable, reproducible outputs where required.

security.trust.definition: Define trust boundaries for users, agents, tools, and data.

security.permissions.definition: Grant the least authority needed for an operation.

security.sandbox.definition: Match isolation claims to tested runtime boundaries.

security.secrets.definition: Keep credentials out of prompts, logs, and repositories.

security.supply_chain.definition: Verify the origin and integrity of dependencies and artifacts.

security.vulnerabilities.definition: Discover, prioritize, and remediate exploitable flaws.

security.audit.definition: Preserve useful records of consequential actions.

security.threat_model.definition: Identify plausible attackers, assets, and failure paths.

security.abuse.definition: Bound misuse of exposed capabilities and outputs.

security.policy.definition: Enforce restrictions with a mechanism that covers the action.

quality.strategy.definition: Choose verification proportional to risk and failure modes.

quality.unit_tests.definition: Check focused behavior with controlled inputs.

quality.integration_tests.definition: Check component boundaries and real dependencies.

quality.end_to_end.definition: Check a complete user or system workflow.

quality.property_tests.definition: Check invariants over varied generated inputs.

quality.evaluations.definition: Grade model or agent outcomes against representative tasks.

quality.benchmarks.definition: Compare performance under controlled, repeatable conditions.

quality.review.definition: Inspect changes for correctness, maintainability, and missed scope.

quality.reproducibility.definition: Preserve enough inputs and environment to repeat a result.

quality.accessibility.definition: Check that people can use the output across abilities and devices.

quality.visual.definition: Inspect rendered or interactive behavior when appearance matters.

delivery.versioning.definition: Communicate compatibility and change through release versions.

delivery.git.definition: Keep change history reviewable and preserve existing work.

delivery.ci.definition: Run deterministic repository gates on shared changes.

delivery.release.definition: Package, publish, and verify a declared version.

delivery.deployment.definition: Move a verified artifact into its operating environment.

delivery.rollback.definition: Recover from a bad release or migration.

delivery.documentation.definition: Give users accurate setup, usage, and limitations.

delivery.artifacts.definition: Produce traceable outputs and evidence of their origin.

operations.observability.definition: Collect signals that explain system behavior and failures.

operations.reliability.definition: Define and check the service behavior that must hold.

operations.incidents.definition: Detect, respond to, and learn from failures.

operations.scheduling.definition: Run recurring work with explicit ownership and failure handling.

operations.monitoring.definition: Watch meaningful conditions and notify the right owner.

operations.resources.definition: Bound compute, storage, network, and financial consumption.

operations.backup.definition: Restore essential state from verified backups.

operations.support.definition: Make diagnosis and correction possible for maintainers and users.

communication.voice.definition: Match tone and persona to audience and task.

communication.anti_slop.definition: Remove generic filler, repetition, and unsupported confidence.

communication.clarity.definition: Explain decisions in plain language with useful structure.

communication.citations.definition: Place a usable source near the claim it supports.

communication.uncertainty.definition: Distinguish observed results, inference, and unknowns.

communication.ux.definition: Make outputs and controls help people decide and act.

communication.visualization.definition: Use a visual when it makes relationships easier to grasp.

context.loadouts.definition: Select a declarative project composition with exact evidence and resource pins.

context.capability_selection.definition: Choose required and optional support for the actual project and stage.

research.confidence.definition: State strength and limitations of claim support without invented probabilities.

quality.comments.definition: Preserve intent, invariants and useful API contracts in accurate comments.

web.design.definition: Choose and critique a coherent visual direction for the product and brand.

web.product.definition: Make audience, primary job and truthful content govern the experience.

web.responsive.definition: Preserve reading order and usable controls across viewport and input sizes.

web.motion.definition: Use bounded purposeful motion with reduced-motion and static fallbacks.

web.performance.definition: Measure assets and interactions without confusing lab and field evidence.

web.static_hosting.definition: Match built routes and runtime features to the actual static destination.
